title.quote: Handling Delay in Reinforcement Learning Caused by Parallel Computations of Neurons
title.justification: The title appears at the beginning of the paper.
title.value: Handling Delay in Reinforcement Learning Caused by Parallel Computations of Neurons

extractions.description: An empirical computational study of reinforcement-learning agents whose neural layers execute in parallel, including delayed-agent training across MuJoCo and MinAtar environments and GPU/CPU inference-speed benchmarks.

type.quote: We perform our main experiments on Mujoco (Todorov et al., 2012) and MiniAtar (Young & Tian, 2019) environments
type.justification: The paper trains and evaluates agents and measures inference speed on hardware.

name.quote: we introduce a new problem in reinforcement learning (RL): training an RL agent in the presence of delay caused by the parallel execution of neurons.
name.justification: The paper explicitly frames its contribution as a reinforcement-learning problem.

name.quote: We explore the trade-off between delay and network expressivity and investigate various types of skip connections to find an optimal balance.
name.justification: Handling delay in neural policies is a central research contribution.

name.quote: Estimating speed-up on modern hardware. ... we demonstrate that significant speed-up can also be achieved on common modern hardware, such as GPU, by executing each layer in parallel.
name.justification: The paper contributes an empirical analysis of parallel neural inference.

name.quote: Moreover, neuromorphic computing inherently utilizes such a speed-up.
name.justification: Neuromorphic computing motivates the setup, but the experiments use conventional GPU and CPU hardware.
